issues.title: Prove real Codex shared control and supported authentication
issues.what: A bounded integration proof connects two minimal clients to one real interactive Codex task on its execution host. Establish the supported provider/version/authentication contract before implementing the production adapter. Human involvement is limited to real test-account access and confirming the offered authentication arrangement; no customer interview is required.
criteria: Demonstrate real task start, streamed output, teammate input delivery, stale-turn rejection, interruption during tool work, one bounded approval resolution, and explicit provider resume. Record provider acknowledgments rather than UI-only success.
Use unique command identities and prove retry deduplication. Distinguish one authoritative approval resolution from any claim of exactly-once external side effects after a crash.

Exercise subscription and API modes separately using authorized test accounts. Document the usage owner and supported multi-human authority; technical login success is not proof of transferable entitlements.

Pin the tested version, record platform prerequisites and capabilities, and provide a runnable acceptance harness and result matrix. A missing required capability produces a concrete supported alternative or blocker.
issues.label: ready-for-human

issues.title: Prove encrypted endpoint enrollment, control and customer recovery
issues.what: Build a desktop/runtime/browser experiment with an established encryption stack: verified endpoints exchange one encrypted task and authenticated control, recover on a clean endpoint, and remove a device. Deliver a reviewed protocol/library decision and threat model, not custom cryptography.
criteria: The relay/database/logs cannot read task content or customer keys; document necessary cleartext metadata and browser/application-code and inference-provider trust boundaries.
An existing trusted endpoint or customer recovery authority verifies new endpoint identity. Test substituted keys, modified controls, replayed approvals, and stale authorization.

Demonstrate clean-endpoint recovery without operator secrets, history scope, membership/key rotation, and future-content exclusion for removed devices; recovery cannot reinstate expired action-approval grants.

Demonstrate supported storage and packaging on both desktop platforms and browser. Record offline/revocation acknowledgment behavior, protocol versions, failure cases, and qualified review requirements. This proof is not a completed production security audit.
issues.label: ready-for-human

issues.title: Install desktop bootstrap builds on macOS and Windows
issues.what: Produce internal installable desktop builds that launch the shared interface and manage the local runtime outside a developer checkout. Connect to a configured remote team service independently from local runtime startup.
criteria: Exercise installation and launch on clean macOS and Windows test environments; no accidental dependency on system Node, a terminal environment, or source-tree paths.
Show runtime readiness and actionable startup failures. Remote-hub configuration still starts and registers the local execution host.
Handle packaged resources, platform-specific paths and project selection; record the exact supported OS/architecture targets and explicit prerequisites.
Provide reproducible internal artifacts and installation evidence. Identify signing/notarization provisioning needed for P19 now; public signed distribution is not required for this internal slice.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Create a private team and pair an explicitly shared execution host
issues.what: Implement a complete account-to-project setup path: authenticate, create a private team, invite a named person, pair an execution host with local approval, and explicitly authorize one project. Treat identity and host authority as distinct from encryption access and billing.
criteria: An owner can create a team, issue an expiring invitation, accept it as another authenticated user, and remove membership; name-only login and caller-supplied roles cannot bypass authorization.
Pairing requires local host consent and selecting an allowed workspace. A remote user cannot register arbitrary paths, claim another runtime, or escalate execution policy.
Direct protocol/HTTP requests enforce account, team, project and host boundaries; outsider history access and foreign runtime routing fail with distinct errors.
Team administration or a paid seat alone grants neither project decryption nor action-approval authority. UI communicates the pending encryption-enrollment state.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Create and reconnect to a durably encrypted task
issues.what: An enrolled endpoint creates a task and reconstructs its content after reconnect through the hosted ciphertext relay. Use a fixture task to make this independently verifiable before connecting the real provider.
criteria: Persist versioned opaque task/event records and encrypted objective, title, messages, plans, tool arguments/results, diffs and activity; cleartext metadata is explicitly enumerated.
Ordered replay restores the full task rather than clearing history and applying only new events. Integrity failures and missing events are visible; duplicate delivery does not duplicate records.
Content-derived server projections, search and file-overlap inspection are moved to authorized endpoints or disabled; no silent plaintext fallback.
Canary content is absent from relay storage, logs and errors. The fixture-based client-to-relay-to-host acceptance path is reusable by later slices.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Run a real Codex task from the installed desktop app
issues.what: From an installed app, configure a supported Codex account, select an authorized repository, and run a useful solo feature task with encrypted activity and changes. Replace the noninteractive-only integration with the validated interactive contract.
criteria: A real provider task executes on the displayed host and workspace, produces file changes, and streams meaningful state through the encrypted task path.
Credentials remain in the provider/host relationship and out of shared descriptors, task content, telemetry and logs; account/version/usage-limit failures are actionable.
Workspace restrictions and actual provider execution capabilities are enforced locally and shown accurately. Remote clients cannot silently increase privileges.
Preserve product task identifiers separately from provider session/turn identifiers. Solo task start does not require another teammate to be online or invited.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Invite a verified teammate into encrypted project history
issues.what: An authorized participant grants an invited teammate access to a project and enrolls that teammate's browser or desktop endpoint, allowing it to reconstruct shared task history. A seeded encrypted task is enough to verify this slice.
criteria: Login and a link alone do not establish cryptographic trust. A trusted endpoint or recovery authority completes the accepted endpoint-verification flow.
Project-level access to existing shared history and future tasks is explained when granted. The teammate can decrypt ordered history and current pending state after joining late.
Uninvited/unverified endpoints cannot read or control tasks through UI or direct requests. A copied private task link never carries decryption authority.
Browser persistence, site-data loss and re-enrollment behavior are explicit and tested. Participant role and pending enrollment states are visible.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Show a sourced, fresh catch-up view for a joining teammate
issues.what: A teammate opens an unfamiliar running task and sees enough verified context to contribute without reading its whole transcript. Build deterministic projections first on an authorized endpoint.
criteria: Show objective, responsible teammate, execution host/provider, current plan/status, recent changes, recorded decisions and current blocker/pending approvals.
Each decision and summary item links to supporting task events or saved artifacts. Distinguish explicitly recorded decisions from inference; do not invent human approval.
Display freshness and disconnected/unknown state. A late join and reconnect produce the same catch-up state as continuous observation.
No server-side plaintext projection is introduced. Generated summaries are optional, do not block completion, and if present run under an authorized customer provider relationship.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Let two teammates steer and interrupt the same running task
issues.what: Alice starts a real task and Bob joins, sends an explicit agent correction and optionally interrupts. Deliver these actions through authenticated encrypted control with provider-confirmed outcomes.
criteria: Near-simultaneous inputs retain actor attribution, stable host acceptance order, unique IDs and queued/delivered/rejected outcomes. A visible message alone is not delivery.
Retries do not redeliver an accepted command; a changed turn rejects stale instructions instead of silently redirecting another turn.
Interrupt shows requested/stopping until runtime/provider acknowledgment; test during tool execution and host disconnection without claiming completed side effects are undone.
Host checks current verified collaborator authority and target task/turn. A human help message is never automatically converted into agent input.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Delegate approval rights and resolve a real action once
issues.what: The execution-host owner explicitly grants Bob action-approval rights; Bob resolves one real pending provider action while Alice sees the same decision and outcome.
criteria: Ordinary collaboration does not confer approval rights. The host validates the current verified actor, grant and exact task/turn/host/action before accepting a response.
Show the exact pending action and its context. Two valid competing responses yield one recorded authoritative resolution; the losing client sees the existing actor and outcome.
Reject mutated actions, replayed or expired responses, stale grants and stale requests after a restart. Deduplicate accepted dispatch without promising general exactly-once shell effects.
Per-action approval is the default. Do not expose broad accept-for-session behavior without bounded, enforced and tested semantics.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Request help from a named teammate through a private inbox
issues.what: A task participant requests help or review from a named authorized project member. The recipient opens the exact task/question from an in-app inbox and explicitly resolves or cancels the request.
criteria: Persist an encrypted question, requester, recipient, task/context references and open/resolved/cancelled state; reject recipients outside the authorized project.
Inbox and task views stay consistent across clients and reconnect. The recipient receives the catch-up context and can act later while host availability remains clear.
Sending a help request produces no provider input or execution. Sending to the agent is a separate explicit action.
No general chat, Slack or email integration is required. Any OS notification is generic and contains no decrypted task text.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Review corrected work and hand over task responsibility
issues.what: Participants inspect the real diff after a teammate correction, record the task outcome, and transfer responsibility to an existing project member with an encrypted note.
criteria: The complete scenario shows an original assumption, confirmed teammate correction, resulting file change and navigable supporting task history.
Handoff changes responsibility only, preserves shared context and clearly displays the unchanged host/workspace/provider usage owner.
The recipient must already have project access. Responsibility does not silently grant approval rights or transfer provider credentials.
Record open/completed/cancelled task outcome independently from individual turn status. Reuse the existing diff experience rather than adding a full editor or Git replacement.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Associate issues and PRs with authorized private task links
issues.what: A project member stores an issue or PR URL with a task and copies a private task link that opens the relevant context only for authorized enrolled recipients.
criteria: Validate supported URL schemes and render links safely. Store the related-work URL encrypted and round-trip it across authorized clients.
A private link routes to authentication, membership checks and endpoint verification; it never reveals task content to an unauthorized visitor.
Adding an association does not read, comment on, or publish task content to the external issue tracker automatically.
Allow adding/removing associations and navigating the task from the same link after reconnect; external tracker integration is not required.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Restore encrypted history on a clean customer device
issues.what: A customer restores the defined project/history and endpoint-trust scope using an existing trusted endpoint or customer-held recovery material, with no operator content-recovery path.
criteria: Exercise recovery on a clean desktop/browser endpoint; wrong material fails, the operator sees only encrypted backups, and all-recovery-method loss is explained honestly.
Protect persisted secrets using the selected supported desktop/browser storage and document site-data/locked-storage failure behavior.
Recovery does not restore expired approval grants or provider credentials. Make the restored scope and trust transitions explicit.
Provide an onboarding recovery exercise and supported replacement/rotation path; do not promise recovery after every trusted endpoint and recovery secret are lost.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Revoke a teammate device without retaining future control
issues.what: A project owner removes access or revokes a device, and participants see the updated encryption/authorization state and each execution host's acknowledgment.
criteria: Advance authenticated membership/key state; removed endpoints cannot decrypt future content under the new state or authorize actions after host application.
Show pending revocation for unreachable hosts. Reconcile current membership before enabling controls after reconnect; do not imply instant knowledge on an offline machine.
Reject substituted identities, replayed grants and stale approval responses. Recovery cannot roll back current authorization.
Explain that already-read plaintext and participant-held history cannot be erased; role, key and paid-seat state remain distinct.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Recover task state after network loss or runtime restart
issues.what: Participants and the execution host recover from browser disconnection, network failure, host sleep, runtime crash and relay restart without losing context or blindly replaying actions.
criteria: Persist enough event/command state to reconcile full prior history, provider lifecycle and pending approvals before controls re-enable.
Distinguish host connectivity from task/turn outcome. Already-started actions may have continued; show their confirmed results or unknown state accurately.
Accepted commands are deduplicated; invalid pending approvals expire. No automatic replay of arbitrary side-effecting commands after uncertain completion.
Use an explicit supported provider resume path; otherwise show recovery-required with an actionable choice. Include reconnect, restart, stale response and crash-window acceptance scenarios.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Keep execution alive in the tray and quit explicitly
issues.what: Closing the app window leaves its execution host alive in the tray/menu bar so an authorized browser participant can continue. Explicit quit communicates and applies the effect on running work.
criteria: Close and reopen the installed window while a real task runs; no duplicate runtime appears and the other client remains able to participate.
Explicit quit warns if tasks are active, confirms the user's intent, shuts down managed processes and reports unavailable state to teammates.
Test platform process cleanup and tray/menu-bar controls. Sleep or lost connectivity is not reported as a successfully completed or stopped task.
Fresh app launch restores connection/setup state without automatically replaying an uncertain task or command.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Execute the complete real collaboration flow on installed Windows
issues.what: Close Windows-specific execution gaps and prove a real task, browser teammate correction, delegated approval, file changes and lifecycle behavior on a clean Windows host.
criteria: Platform-aware shell invocation, binary discovery, command shims, drive-letter/project paths and process-tree interruption work in the documented execution environment.
Any required provider execution environment is explicitly guided and tested; no hidden prerequisite or substitution of browser access for Windows host execution.
Installed project selection, provider setup, actual changes, remote controls, close/reopen and explicit quit pass on recorded Windows versions.
Preserve the passing macOS workflow with focused cross-platform checks; do not infer native support solely from a packaged installer.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Ship signed installers with a tested upgrade and recovery path
issues.what: Produce trustworthy macOS/Windows distribution artifacts and verify upgrade/reinstall/rollback behavior without stranding runtime state, encrypted history or credentials. Human work covers signing accounts/credentials and installed-build review.
criteria: Provision and protect required signing/notarization credentials; produce reproducible artifacts and validate clean-machine install without a developer shell.
Load trusted packaged application code, isolate/sandbox renderers as appropriate and narrowly validate privileged IPC; the production desktop must not rely on arbitrary remote renderer privileges.
Test upgrade compatibility for runtime/provider versions, encrypted storage and pending work. Document unsupported downgrades and a recoverable reinstall/rollback procedure.
Manual update delivery is acceptable initially if clear and verified. Begin provisioning alongside P03 rather than waiting for all runtime features to finish.
issues.label: ready-for-human

issues.title: Provide content-safe onboarding diagnostics and support
issues.what: Provide a first-run checklist, clear setup/recovery errors and an explicitly reviewed diagnostic export so founders can assist pilot teams without receiving their private code or secrets.
criteria: Guide account, endpoint enrollment, project/host pairing, provider readiness, first solo task and teammate invitation with actionable stage-specific failures.
Diagnostics include only necessary versions, capability/error identifiers and redacted health state; exclude prompts, paths/repository names, diffs, tool content, keys and credentials.
Users can inspect the export before sharing; the product does not automatically send it externally. Document privacy/metadata and recovery-loss boundaries plainly.
Exercise successful onboarding plus representative unsupported-account, missing-runtime, failed-enrollment and recovery errors through installed and browser clients.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Delete shared tasks and offboard projects with explicit retention
issues.what: An authorized customer deletes task/project records and offboards access, with understandable live-storage, index, backup and participant-copy behavior.
criteria: Remove deleted ciphertext and routing/index references from live stores; deny subsequent fetch/control requests and reflect deletion in authorized clients.
Publish and implement a bounded backup retention/deletion policy before external release; service restore must not silently reactivate deleted memberships or control grants.
Apply related access/key revocation without conflating history deletion with erasing participant-held plaintext or copies.
Test unauthorized deletion, concurrent access, reconnect and restore paths; logs/support exports cannot resurrect deleted content.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Measure setup, catch-up and real collaboration without task content
issues.what: Implement disclosed content-free measurement from actual endpoint/runtime outcomes, making setup failures, viewing/help, delivered intervention, task completion and returning-team behavior separately visible.
criteria: Count an activated person only after a qualifying task has two distinct participating humans and a non-initiator's intervention confirmed delivered; participation means task start or authenticated control/approval action.
Do not count signup, passive views, help requests or queued-but-undelivered input as activation. Retry deduplication prevents duplicate person/task/event counts.
Collect setup-stage outcomes, useful solo starts, invites, catch-up/help, direct control, completion and later-week team return without prompts, titles, paths, URLs, diffs or tool content.

Compute/emit minimal events at authorized endpoints rather than inspecting relay plaintext. Implement disclosure, retention/deletion and a test path covering solo and two-person tasks; interviews are not required.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Manage individual paid pilot seats separately from project access
issues.what: Provide founder-operated individual seat entitlement records and customer-visible billing boundaries, allowing paid pilot operations without building automated checkout or deciding a price now.
criteria: Grant/revoke individual entitlements and record payment/owner status; team, project, decryption and approval rights remain independently enforced.
Price is configured or recorded later. No invented price, free-reviewer tier, pricing interview or payment is a prerequisite for implementation.
Separate product seats from customer provider usage. Distinguish actual paid teams from free pilots, verbal intent and unpaid invoices.
Test entitlement changes and billing/access separation. Do not initiate charges or customer messages as part of this implementation issue.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Verify the Codex release on both platforms and its privacy boundary
issues.what: Run the complete installed desktop/browser product through the parent spec's single acceptance boundary, including an independent implementation/threat-model review, and produce the external Codex release go/no-go. Customer interviews are not a gate.
criteria: On both advertised execution platforms, two users complete encrypted join/catch-up, real correction, bounded delegated approval, diff review, help/handoff, private links and background/quit behavior.
Exercise unauthorized endpoints, malicious relay/replay, stale grants, revocation, clean-device recovery, runtime/network interruption and supported resume. Record provider/auth/version support.

Complete independent review of implemented privacy and control; inspect live/backup stores, logs, telemetry, notifications and diagnostics for canary plaintext. Claims accurately reflect reviewed scope.

Confirm usable installed distribution, upgrade/recovery, onboarding/support, documented metadata/retention and service restore. A failed core technical requirement blocks external release and names a concrete remedy, not an interview prerequisite.
issues.label: ready-for-human

issues.title: Prove Claude Code authentication and collaborative controls
issues.what: Exercise a real Claude integration against the common adapter contract and select the supported SDK/binary and authentication arrangement. Human involvement covers test-account access and any required provider authorization.
criteria: Verify actual queued input versus live steering, interruption, permission callbacks, resume and platform prerequisites; do not equate session resume with adopting any existing running native session.
Establish the allowed customer subscription/API arrangement for this product; do not assume personal subscription credentials can be routed through an SDK product.
Produce a versioned capability/auth/platform matrix and runnable acceptance evidence; choose a supported path and explicitly identify any required core behavior that cannot be met.
Run early once the common contract is stable; this proof does not block the first Codex release and requires no customer interview.
issues.label: ready-for-human

issues.title: Release Claude Code through the encrypted team workflow
issues.what: Add Claude as a selectable provider with the same project/enrollment permissions, catch-up, shared task view and truthful delivery states using the validated path.
criteria: Real two-human tasks pass the advertised steering/queuing, required approval, interruption and supported resume behavior on advertised platforms/auth modes.
Unsupported or queued outcomes are labeled accurately; never enable a control that silently does something different or has no provider effect.
E2EE, current membership/grants, replay/recovery, credentials and content-free telemetry preserve the common boundaries.
Run focused Codex regressions and publish setup/limitations and provider-version support. If a core promise fails, resolve the scope/implementation conflict instead of advertising parity.
issues.label: ready-for-agent

issues.title: Prove Cursor authentication and collaborative controls
issues.what: Exercise real Cursor ACP/SDK candidates and choose the interface satisfying this product's shared-control and delegated-approval contract. Human involvement covers test accounts and any required provider authorization.
criteria: Test actual local steering versus follow-up, cancellation, permission requests and resume; distinguish ACP, local SDK, detached/cloud runs and native IDE session adoption.
Verify customer account/billing support, platform prerequisites and provider versions without assuming transferable subscriptions.
Return a runnable experiment, a selected integration path and capability/auth/platform matrix; unsupported required behavior is an explicit implementation/scope blocker.
Can proceed alongside the Claude proof after the common contract is stable; it does not block the Codex release or require a customer interview.
issues.label: ready-for-human

issues.title: Release Cursor through the encrypted team workflow
issues.what: Add Cursor using the verified integration path and the same private project, encrypted history, catch-up, control and handoff experience.
criteria: Advertised controls produce real provider outcomes during a two-human task on supported platforms/auth modes; queued/follow-up/unsupported actions remain distinct.
Preserve membership, delegated approvals, encryption/key handling, credential boundaries, reconnect/recovery and minimal telemetry.
Publish setup, versions and limitations after passing the applicable shared release checks; do not claim existing native-chat takeover or cross-provider execution migration.
Run focused regressions for existing providers. The Claude release is not a technical dependency; release order follows validated engineering readiness.
issues.label: ready-for-agent
